title: Reading demand and supply curves
examples: Why does the demand curve slope down?
How do you read a supply and demand graph?

explain.say: Here is a riddle: why do shops have sales? Economists answer with two simple lines. Look at the board: the demand curve. Price goes up the side, and quantity, which means how many, goes along the bottom.

marks.label: Low price, many buy
marks.ask: What makes a demand curve shift?

explain.say: See the mark high on the left? When bubble tea costs a lot, few people buy it. Now follow the line down to the right: as the price falls, more people buy. That is the law of demand. Does that match what you do?

marks.label: Low price, many buy
marks.ask: What makes a demand curve shift?

explain.say: Now the supply curve. It slopes the other way. At a low price, few cafes bother selling bubble tea; at a high price, more open up to make money. That is the law of supply. Can you see why this line rises?

marks.label: Low price, few sold
marks.ask: What is the law of supply?

marks.label: High price, many sold
marks.ask: What is the law of supply?

explain.say: Put the two lines together and they cross at one point, the equilibrium, which means balance. Look at the steps: if the price is too high, unsold drinks pile up, so sellers cut the price until buyers and sellers match.

stages.label: Sellers cut price
stages.note: A sale to clear the stock.

explain.say: Now you can read a sale sign like an economist: the price was above the balance point! Excellent work! Wow: Alfred Marshall drew these crossing curves in 1890, and they are still the first diagram in economics classes worldwide.

faq.q: What is the law of demand?
faq.a: The law of demand says that when the price of something falls, people buy more of it, and when the price rises, they buy less, if nothing else changes.

faq.q: What is the law of supply?
faq.a: The law of supply says that when the price rises, sellers offer more, because making and selling it becomes more profitable.
Equilibrium is where the demand and supply curves cross: the price at which the amount people want to buy equals the amount sellers offer.

faq.q: What makes a demand curve shift?
faq.a: Changes other than price, such as income, fashion, the weather or the price of similar goods. A heat wave shifts demand for cold drinks to the right.

faq.q: Why is price on the vertical axis?
faq.a: It is a habit started by Alfred Marshall's diagrams in 1890. Mathematicians would usually put price along the bottom, but economists kept Marshall's way.
asks: Why are supply and demand graphs drawn that way?

facts: Alfred Marshall popularised the supply and demand diagram in Principles of Economics (1890).
A demand curve usually slopes downward and a supply curve usually slopes upward.

quiz.say: What does a downward-sloping demand curve show?
quiz.show: What does a downward-sloping demand curve show?
quiz.why: As price falls, quantity demanded rises.

wrong.0: That is backwards; higher prices usually mean fewer buyers.
wrong.2: The curve shows how buying changes as price changes.
